description: Turn callHermesStream in backend/internal/bridge/hermes.go into a multi-turn OpenAI-style function-calling loop that declares read_file, write_file and patch_file, executes them locally against WORKSPACE_DIR, feeds the results back to Hermes and re-requests until the model replies with text only. Tools are declared ONLY when mode == "desk". The loop must degrade to exactly today's single-turn behaviour when Hermes never returns tool_calls, and must log one greppable diagnostic per job saying whether tool calls were seen. This is the whole backend of the task; FEAT-003 (frontend labels) is independent of it.
steps: Read backend/internal/bridge/hermes.go end to end first. Reuse b.workDir and b.safePath — do NOT add a second path validator. Do NOT touch backend/internal/bridge/pi.go. Do NOT remove handleToolFileWrite / writeToolNames (the v1.9.0 opportunistic write interception) nor its mode=="desk" gate: it stays as the fallback for models that only emit hermes.tool.progress.

Define the tool schema table in hermes.go: a package-level slice of OpenAI-style tool declarations (type:"function", function:{name, description, parameters:{type:"object", properties, required}}) for exactly three tools. read_file{path}. write_file{path, content}. patch_file{path, old_string, new_string}. Write the descriptions in French, aimed at Lya, and state in read_file's description that content may be truncated and in patch_file's that old_string must appear exactly once.

Choose and document the patch shape: old_string/new_string exact replacement, with a doc comment on the tool explaining why (simplest shape a model reliably produces; unified diff would need fuzzy hunk matching). Rules: if old_string is absent from the file, return an error result 'old_string introuvable'; if it occurs more than once, return an error result naming the number of occurrences and asking for a longer, unique old_string; never silently no-op, never write the file in either case.

Add package-level constants next to the tool table: maxToolLoops = 8, maxReadFileChars = 20000 (mirror the frontend MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS cap in Chat.tsx and say so in the comment), and allowedWriteExts = {".md", ".json", ".txt"} (the extensions the app itself handles, see backend/internal/api/files.go and the editor).

Implement the three executors as methods on *HermesBridge, each taking the decoded arguments and returning (resultString string, changedPath string, err error) or an equivalent struct. readFileTool: safePath, os.ReadFile, truncate to maxReadFileChars and append an explicit truncation notice when cut. writeFileTool: safePath, reject an extension not in allowedWriteExts, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir, 0755), os.WriteFile(..., 0644), return the byte count and the relative path as changedPath. patchFileTool: safePath, extension check, os.ReadFile, strings.Count for occurrence checking, strings.Replace once, write back with 0644, return changedPath. Every failure must be returned as a readable error message the model can act on, never a panic and never a job-level error event.

Refactor callHermesStream: keep its signature (ctx, job, content, systemPrompt, mode) so startJob is unchanged. Build messages as []map[string]interface{} (tool messages need a tool_call_id field, so the current []map[string]string no longer fits) with the same [system?, user] start as today. Then loop up to maxToolLoops iterations: each iteration marshals {messages, provider:"custom", stream:true} plus "tools": hermesFileTools and "tool_choice":"auto" ONLY when mode == "desk" && b.workDir != "", performs the POST with the existing headers/auth handling and error mapping (keep the auth-failure log, the keyFingerprint diagnostic and the French error strings byte-for-byte), and consumes the SSE stream.

Extract the SSE consumption into a helper (for example func (b *HermesBridge) streamTurn(job *Job, body io.Reader, mode string, full *strings.Builder) (turnResult, error)) so the loop body stays readable. It must keep every current behaviour: skip blank lines and ':' comments, track 'event:' names, forward hermes.tool.progress frames verbatim as StreamEvent{Type:"tool"} and run handleToolFileWrite + file_changed emission when mode=="desk", surface chunk.error as StreamEvent{Type:"error"}, and stream every non-empty delta.content as StreamEvent{Type:"delta"} while accumulating into full.

Extend the chunk struct in that helper to also decode choices[].delta.tool_calls[] with fields index, id, type and function{name, arguments}, plus choices[].finish_reason. Accumulate tool-call deltas by index into a slice: id and function.name arrive once (usually on the first delta for that index), function.arguments arrive as a string fragment stream that must be concatenated. Treat 'data: [DONE]' as end-of-turn, not end-of-job: only append StreamEvent{Type:"done", Reply: full.String()} when the finished turn carried no tool calls.

After a turn that carried tool calls: append the assistant message {role:"assistant", content: <text of that turn, may be empty>, tool_calls: [...]} to messages, then for each accumulated call emit StreamEvent{Type:"tool", Tool: map{name, path, status:"running"}} before execution and a second one with status:"done" (or status:"error" plus the message) after, json.Unmarshal the accumulated arguments string (a malformed JSON payload is a tool error returned to the model, not a job failure), dispatch to the matching executor, refuse an unknown tool name with an error result, and append {role:"tool", tool_call_id: <id>, content: <result or error text>} to messages. Emit the synthetic StreamEvent{Type:"tool", Tool: map{"name":"file_changed", "path": changedPath}} after every successful write_file or patch_file, matching the shape already emitted in the v1.9.0 path so Chat.tsx reloads the editor.

Gate hard on mode: when mode != "desk" no tools are declared in the request body, and even if a model returned tool_calls anyway they must NOT be executed. In that case terminate the turn as today (emit done with the accumulated text) and log the refusal. TestHermesBridge_FileWrite_LyaMode must stay green.

Loop cap: when maxToolLoops iterations have run and the model still asks for tools, stop, emit a delta with a short French terminal message telling the teacher the tool loop was cut short, then emit StreamEvent{Type:"done", Reply: full.String()} and return nil. The job must never hang; jobRunTimeout (10 min) still applies via ctx.

Diagnostics: log exactly one greppable line per job of the form 'hermes: tool_calls supported=true|false (mode=%s loops=%d toolCalls=%d)' where supported is true iff at least one tool_calls delta was received during the job. Also log one line per executed tool with its name, path and outcome. Add a doc comment above the tool table stating plainly that whether Hermes forwards the `tools` parameter to the upstream model is unverified from a sandbox and that this log line is how it gets settled in production.

Extend backend/internal/bridge/hermes_test.go following the existing mockHermesServer / mockHermesFileWriteServer style. Add a configurable fake that serves a scripted sequence of turns (one entry per request: either tool_calls deltas or plain text) and records every decoded request body so tests can assert on the `tools` array and on the tool result messages fed back. Tests to add: (a) read_file round-trip — first turn asks read_file on a file seeded in t.TempDir(), second turn returns text; assert the second request contains a role:"tool" message carrying the file content and that the final done.Reply is the text; (b) write_file round-trip — assert the file exists on disk with the right bytes and that a file_changed tool event was emitted; (c) patch_file success — assert only the targeted substring changed and the rest of the file is intact; (d) patch_file old_string not found — assert the file is unchanged, the tool result fed back contains the failure, no error StreamEvent is emitted and the job still reaches done; (e) patch_file ambiguous old_string (2 occurrences) — same expectations, file unchanged; (f) path traversal ('../../etc/passwd') rejected for read_file, write_file and patch_file; (g) disallowed extension ('notes.exe' or 'x.sh') rejected by write_file and patch_file with an error result; (h) loop cap — fake that always returns the same tool call; assert the job terminates with done within the test timeout and that the fake received exactly maxToolLoops requests; (i) mode lya — assert the request body contains no `tools` key and no file is written; (j) degradation — fake that ignores `tools` and streams only text deltas; assert exactly the pre-existing behaviour (deltas forwarded, done.Reply complete, no error, one single request).

Verify by mutation before declaring done: for each of read_file truncation, write_file extension check, patch_file not-found, patch_file ambiguity, path traversal, loop cap and the lya gate, temporarily reintroduce the bug (or delete the guard), run go test, confirm the matching test FAILS, then restore. Record in findings which test caught which mutation.

Run gofmt -l . and fix any formatting before committing. Commit with a conventional message, for example 'feat: multi-turn Hermes tool loop with read_file, write_file and patch_file in mode Desk'. Do not push, do not touch version.json.
acceptance_criteria: cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . && go test ./... -count=1 -timeout=90s passes with no gofmt output
A read_file tool call from a fake Hermes results in the file content being appended to messages as a role:"tool" message and the following turn's text reaching the client as deltas plus a done event
write_file creates parent directories, writes the file inside the temp workspace and emits a tool event {name:"file_changed", path:...}

patch_file applies a targeted old_string to new_string replacement, and returns an error result to the model (leaving the file untouched, no error StreamEvent, job still reaches done) when old_string is missing or occurs more than once
Path traversal is rejected for all three tools and no file is created or read outside the workspace root
write_file and patch_file reject extensions outside .md, .json and .txt with an error result the model receives
A fake Hermes that always returns a tool call causes the job to terminate after exactly maxToolLoops requests with a done event and a French terminal message, not a hang
In mode lya the request body contains no tools key, no tool is executed, no file is written, and TestHermesBridge_FileWrite_LyaMode still passes
A fake Hermes that ignores tools and returns only text produces exactly the pre-v-change behaviour: one HTTP request, all deltas forwarded, done.Reply complete, no error event
One log line per job matches 'hermes: tool_calls supported=' with true or false
buildDeskPrompt and MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS in frontend/src/components/Chat.tsx are unchanged, and backend/internal/bridge/pi.go is unchanged (git diff shows no modification to either)
No code comment, commit message or doc claims the tool loop was verified against the real Hermes gateway
verification: cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . && go test ./... -count=1 -timeout=90s
git diff --stat main -- backend/internal/bridge/pi.go frontend/src/components/Chat.tsx (must show no changes to pi.go, and no change to buildDeskPrompt if Chat.tsx appears at all)
cd frontend && npx vitest --run && npm run build
